name: Micron Technology, Inc.
monetization: Sells DRAM, HBM, and NAND — the US-based HBM supplier, with capacity sold out and revenue up ~4.5× y/y at super-cycle pricing.
description_md: Micron is the only US-headquartered maker of DRAM and HBM, the third leg of the HBM triopoly with SK hynix and Samsung. The AI memory super-cycle transformed its P&L faster than any large-cap semiconductor company on record: fiscal Q3 2026 (ended May 2026) revenue was $41.5B versus $9.3B in the same quarter a year earlier, with fiscal Q4 guided to ~$50B at ~86% gross margin. Its HBM output is sold out through calendar 2026, with supply agreements to Nvidia and other accelerator programs; during 2025–26 some share trackers placed Micron ahead of Samsung in HBM.
ai_monetization_md: HBM3E/HBM4 for AI accelerators plus high-capacity server DRAM (including LP server memory) and enterprise/data-center NAND — all at bottleneck pricing, with customers signing long-term agreements and HBM sold out through calendar 2026. The revenue trajectory ($9.3B → $41.5B y/y for FQ3; ~$50B guided at ~86% GM) reflects both volume and unprecedented price: memory is capturing a historically large share of AI-system bill-of-materials value. US-based manufacturing (Idaho/New York expansions, CHIPS support) positions Micron as the domestic-content HBM option for US buildouts.
ai_strategy_md: Ramp HBM4 with capacity discipline: management has prioritized long-term agreements and profitability over share-chasing, converting sold-out conditions into multi-year visibility. Expand US fabs (Boise, Clay NY) under CHIPS incentives to own the 'secure US memory supply' position as sovereign/defense AI programs grow. The strategic risk it manages is the classic memory trap — over-adding capacity at the top of a super-cycle.
risk_notes_md: **Super-cycle sustainability:** ~86% guided gross margin is far outside memory's historical band (typically negative to ~60%); a demand pause or HBM supply catch-up (Samsung, CXMT at trailing edge) would compress it violently — Micron carries the highest earnings beta to the cycle of the three HBM makers. **Concentration:** AI accelerator programs (Nvidia foremost) dominate HBM demand. **Capex escalation:** meeting sold-out demand requires record capex into 2027, spent at peak equipment prices. Historical base rate: every prior memory super-cycle ended in a glut.

events.title: FQ3-2026: revenue $41.5B vs $9.3B a year earlier; FQ4 guided to ~$50B at ~86% GM
events.why_it_matters: The single most extreme y/y revenue expansion of the AI cycle among large caps — direct evidence of how much buildout capex is flowing to the HBM/DRAM bottleneck.
